```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
data=davisdata
```
 Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
 you choose to sit in??

# Introduction 
The question is this: Is there a relationship between where you sit in class and how much you drink?  
data from UCDavis math 116 class  
$H_0$  is there is no relationship what row in class sit and how much you drink.  
$H_A$  there is a difference in what row in class you sit and how much you drink.   


# Methods 
Seat is catagorical  
Alcohol is numerical


# data summary's 



## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
boxplot(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```
  
  Graph demonstrates that if the student sit in the back they are more likely to consume more ounces of alcohol per week than those who sit in the front or middle. 
 



## Numerical Summary 

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=ucdavis1)
```

The numerical summary shows us that the students who sit in the back of the class drinks aboout 10 more ounces of alcohol per week than those in the middle and and front.  

## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```
The p value is 0.000116 which is less than 0.05 so we fail to reject the $H_0$ and conclude that there is a relationship between students who sit in the back and the consumption of ounces of alcohol per week.

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```
The tukey graph shows there is a difference in alcohol consumption between student who sit in the front and back and middle and back. There is no difference in alchohol consumption between the front and middle rows. 

## Conclusions
The question was if there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row you choose to sit in and there is a difference between those who sat in the back consumed more alcohol than those in the front or middle rows.
